docs_page.cli_intro: Install any community skill locally with a single `skills` command.
docs_page.cli_prereq_p1: Install Node.js from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org) (it ships with `npm`), then verify:
docs_page.cli_login_p1: First generate a token at [{site}/settings/tokens]({site}/settings/tokens) (it is shown only once — copy it right away), then:
docs_page.cli_login_p2: After logging in, every command targets this site by default — no need to pass `--registry` again.
docs_page.cli_install_p1: Every skill's detail page has an "Install" box pre-filled with `skills install '<slug>'` — just copy and run. Restricted skills must be requested first: click "Request download" on the detail page and wait for the author's approval before installing.
docs_page.cli_install_p2: Packs are admin-curated skill bundles organized by scenario (see the "Packs" tab on the browse page); a single `pack:` command installs them all — if one item fails (e.g. restricted and not yet approved), the rest still install.
docs_page.cli_upgrade_p1: When the site ships a new CLI version (e.g. adding `pack:` pack installs), upgrade with one command:
docs_page.cli_upgrade_p2: Note the difference: `skills update` updates **the skills you have installed**; `skills upgrade` upgrades the `skills` **command itself**.
docs_page.cli_upgrade_p3: If your CLI is too old to have the `upgrade` command yet, just reinstall it once manually (it will be available afterwards):
docs_page.cli_uninstall_p1: Uninstalling the CLI does not touch the skill files already installed locally. To remove a skill, just delete its directory: `.claude/skills/'<slug>'/` inside a project, `~/.claude/skills/'<slug>'/` globally.
docs_page.authoring_intro: Every skill is essentially a `SKILL.md` file — a block of YAML frontmatter at the top, followed by a Markdown body written for Claude.
docs_page.authoring_frontmatter_table:
| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | ✓ | Skill name, shown on the card |
| `description` | ✓ | One-line description, 140 characters max |
| `version` | ✓ | Follows semver, e.g. 1.2.0 |
| `license` |  | Defaults to MIT |
| `triggers` |  | Keywords that make Claude auto-activate this skill |
| `dependencies` |  | Slugs of other skills it depends on, comma-separated |
docs_page.authoring_h_tips: 3. Tips for writing a good body
docs_page.authoring_tip_1: **Say how to do it, directly.** A skill is written for Claude, not marketing copy for humans. State its core capability in the very first paragraph.
docs_page.authoring_tip_2: **List trigger conditions separately** so Claude can tell at a glance when to use the skill.
docs_page.authoring_tip_3: **Do not write a prompt prefix** (like "You are playing the role of…"). Claude is already acting as an agent and does not need to be "commanded" — write the rules and workflow directly.
docs_page.authoring_tip_4: **Put examples last.** If you have input/output examples, place them at the end of the skill under a `## Examples` heading.
docs_page.authoring_length_table:
| Token range | Suited for |
|---|---|
| < 800 | Micro utilities — simple prompt rewrites, format checks |
| 800-2K | Standard skills — most use cases |
| 2K-5K | Complex skills — multi-step workflows + multiple trigger scenarios |
| > 5K | Not recommended — split into several skills that cooperate via composition |
docs_page.authoring_length_note: The platform shows the token cost you declare (entered manually at creation) on the skill card, so users can pick accordingly.
docs_page.authoring_upload_form: **Form mode**: fill in the form on the site and write the Markdown body directly — good for simple skills
docs_page.authoring_upload_pack: **Package mode**: upload a zip (containing SKILL.md plus optional script files) — good for skills that ship helper scripts
docs_page.authoring_upload_note: Either way, you can edit and publish new versions after uploading (semver, strictly increasing); subscribers get an update notice.
docs_page.authoring_remix_1: **Credit the source** in your forked skill — e.g. "based on `xxxxx`"
docs_page.authoring_remix_2: If the original license has requirements, keep it (permissive licenses like MIT impose none)
docs_page.authoring_remix_3: For major changes, rename the skill and position it as its own thing instead of confusing people with a near-identical name

docs_page.start_intro: From no account to your first Skill installed locally, in five steps. You need a browser, Node.js with `npm` already installed, and a target project directory.
docs_page.start_account_p1: Self-service registration is closed. On the intranet deploy, sign in with your W3 account — the account is created on first login. Otherwise ask a site administrator to create one for you.
docs_page.start_account_rules:
| Item | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| How you get one | W3 first login creates it; email/password accounts are created by an administrator |
| Display name | 2–64 characters, editable later under Settings |
| Handle | Derived from the part of the email before `@` (lowercased, non-alphanumerics become `-`, max 24 chars). Not user-chosen |
docs_page.start_account_note: After signing in you land back on the page you came from — so you can share any in-site link with a colleague who is not signed in yet, and they end up in the same place.
docs_page.start_w3_p1: On the intranet deployment, `/auth/login` shows a 「Huawei W3 SSO」 card next to 「Email & password」. Click 「Sign in with W3」 to go through company authentication; the first login creates the account automatically, so there is no registration step.
docs_page.start_w3_p2: A W3 account has no local password: email sign-in only returns 「Invalid email or password」, and you cannot set one — 「Settings」 → 「Security」 shows 「W3 account: authentication is managed by the company — no local password.」 If an account with the same email already exists, W3 sign-in links to it and both methods then work.
docs_page.start_w3_p3: If that card is missing from the sign-in page, this deploy has W3 disabled — accounts can then only be created by an administrator.
docs_page.start_cli_p1: Open [The skills CLI](/docs/cli) and run the `npm i -g …/skills-cli.tgz` command from 「1. Install the CLI (one-time)」 — the site address is already filled in there.
docs_page.start_cli_p2: Verify with `skills --version`: any output means it is installed. That command always prints `0.1.0`, unrelated to the released package version — do not use it to compare versions.
docs_page.start_token_1: Avatar menu → 「Settings」 → 「CLI Token」 in the left sidebar, i.e. `/settings/tokens`.
docs_page.start_token_2: Type a name (1–60 characters) in 「New token name (e.g. laptop, ci-server)」 and click 「Generate」.
docs_page.start_token_3: The token looks like `scm_pat_…` and is shown once, at creation. Click 「Copy」 and save it immediately; once the notice is dismissed it cannot be retrieved — generate a new one instead.
docs_page.start_token_4: Tokens have no expiry; they stay valid until you click 「Revoke」 on their row, which immediately kills every CLI session using them.
docs_page.start_login_registry: Replace `'<registry>'` with the full address of this site, path prefix included — on the intranet that is `https://cari.rnd.huawei.com/ai-community`. Without `--registry` the CLI uses a built-in default address and may talk to a different server.
docs_page.start_login_p2: The command stops at a `Token: ` prompt — paste the token and press Enter. It must start with `scm_pat_`, otherwise the CLI reports a format error and exits.
docs_page.start_login_p3: The token and the address are written to `~/.skills/config.json` (mode 600), so later commands need no `--registry`. To target another address for one command, the global flag must come before the subcommand: `skills --registry '<url>' install '<slug>'`. After the subcommand it is rejected.
docs_page.start_install_p1: On any Skill detail page click 「Copy」 in the install box, `cd` into the target project, then run:
docs_page.start_install_paths:
| Where you run it | Installs into |
| --- | --- |
| A `.git` directory exists above the working directory | `'<git root>'/.claude/skills/'<slug>'/` |
| Command includes `-g` | `~/.claude/skills/'<slug>'/` |
| No `.git` above the working directory | The current directory; the output marks it as non-git |
docs_page.start_install_p2: On success the output is `✔ 安装 '<slug>'@'<version>'` plus the install path. A `⚠ checksum` warning means the files were written but may be incomplete — run the install again.
docs_page.start_zip_p1: Below the install box, click 「Download skill bundle (.zip)」 and unzip it into `~/.claude/skills/'<slug>'/`.
docs_page.start_zip_p2: When you are signed out that control is a sign-in link: it sends you to the login page first, then back to the same detail page.
docs_page.start_rules_login: Every download requires being signed in, public Skills included; anonymous web downloads and CLI calls both get 401.
docs_page.start_rules_restricted: A Skill marked 「Restricted download」 must be requested first: on its detail page add an optional reason (500 characters max), click 「Request download」 and wait for the author. Requests can only be submitted on the web, not from the CLI.
docs_page.start_rules_private: Private and unpublished Skills always return 404; their existence is never revealed.
docs_page.start_rules_cli_off: An admin can switch off CLI access for an account. Every existing CLI token on that account stops working immediately and all commands report that sign-in is required.
docs_page.start_rules_cap_intro: The download cap is set per account and only an admin can change it. The window is a rolling 24 hours, not a calendar day; over the cap the server returns 429. Skill owners and admins are exempt.
docs_page.start_rules_cap_table:
| Cap | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Left blank | Unlimited |
| Greater than 0 | At most that many downloads per rolling 24 hours; over the cap the web UI shows a red message and the CLI prints the same text, stating the cap and the 24-hour window |
| 0 | Downloading is blocked outright; the message states that your cap is 0 and to ask an admin to change it |
docs_page.start_faq_table:
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The CLI prints 「✗ 不是合法的 token 格式（应以 scm_pat_ 开头）」 | What you pasted is not a CLI token from this site, or characters were lost while copying | Go back to 「Settings」 → 「CLI Token」, 「Generate」 a new one and copy the whole `scm_pat_…` string |
| Email sign-in keeps returning 「Invalid email or password」 | That address is a W3 account and has no local password | Use 「Sign in with W3」; a W3 account cannot be given a local password |
| A download returns 401 or asks you to sign in | Signed out in the browser; or the CLI token was revoked, or CLI access was switched off for the account | Sign in on the web; for the CLI, generate a new token and run `skills login` again |
| A download returns 429 | The cap for the rolling 24-hour window is used up | Wait for the window to slide, or ask an admin to raise the cap |
| `skills install` says the Skill does not exist, or clearly hits another server | `skills login --registry` was never run, so the CLI uses its built-in default address | Run `skills login --registry` again with the full site address, path prefix included |

docs_page.publish_intro: Upload a Skill, control who can download it, publish new versions, Remix someone else's Skill, and install packs. Every download requires a login.
docs_page.publish_entry_1: The 「上传 Skill」 button at the top right of the 「浏览 Skills」 page is the primary upload entry. Neither the navbar nor the user menu has one; the home page 「发布 Skill」 button and the 「来发布第一个」 link in an empty skill grid open the same form.
docs_page.publish_entry_2: 「发布新 Skill」 at the top of your Workspace (the profile tab only you can see) opens the same form. If you are not signed in, you go through the login page first and land back on the form.
docs_page.publish_entry_3: Two submit buttons sit at the bottom of the form: 「发布」 publishes and lands on the Skill detail page; 「存为草稿」 saves and lands on the manage panel. A draft is visible only to you and to administrators.
docs_page.publish_fields_table:
| Field | Required | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 上传文件 | Yes | Must contain `SKILL.md`; without it the 「发布」 button stays disabled |
| 名称 | Yes | Validated together with 「一行描述」; neither may be empty |
| 一行描述 | Yes | 140 characters max |
| 来源分类 | Yes | Pick one of 外部 / 官方搬运 / 内部 |
| 类别 | No | Left empty means 「未分类」 |
| Overview / 公开简介 | No | Body of the 「概览」 tab, 50000 characters max |
| 标签 | No | Comma or newline separated |
| 可见性 / 访问权限 | No | Defaults to 「公开」 |
| Slug | No | Derived from the name if empty: lowercase, 64 characters max; immutable after creation |
| 触发词 | No | Under 「高级选项」 |
| 许可证 | No | Defaults to MIT |
| Token 成本 | No | 0 to 50000; left empty, the server estimates it from the `SKILL.md` body |
docs_page.publish_fields_prefill: Once files are staged, the frontmatter of the first `SKILL.md` fills the fields that are still empty: `name` into 名称 and Slug, `description` into 一行描述, `triggers` into 触发词, `license` only while 许可证 is still the default MIT. Fields you already filled are never overwritten.
docs_page.publish_fields_ai: 「AI 一键补全空字段」 and the per-field AI buttons write only into fields that are currently empty. They require a server-side AI configuration and a staged `SKILL.md`; otherwise they stay disabled. Each account is capped at 60 AI calls per hour, after which the call is rate-limited.
docs_page.publish_fields_readme: When the package contains a README, 「用上传包里的 README.md 作为 Overview」 appears and is ticked by default, which replaces the Overview editor with a notice. Untick it to write your own Overview. The content of `SKILL.md` is never used as the public Overview.
docs_page.publish_package_1: The 「上传文件」 area accepts dragged files and folders, 「选择文件」, and 「选择文件夹」. A dropped or picked .zip is unpacked in the browser into the staged list; when a path repeats, the later entry wins.
docs_page.publish_package_2: The packed upload limit is 512 MB. The 5 MB figure in the dropzone hint is stale copy, not the real cap.
docs_page.publish_package_3: No file-type allowlist applies inside the package. A text file longer than 8,388,608 characters is stored truncated and the 「文件」 tab shows 「文件过大，已截断显示」.
docs_page.publish_reject_table:
| Rejection cause | Message |
| --- | --- |
| No `SKILL.md` at any depth in the package (case-insensitive) | 解析失败：Bundle does not contain a SKILL.md file |
| `SKILL.md` does not start with YAML frontmatter | 解析失败：SKILL.md is missing YAML frontmatter |
| Frontmatter is not a valid YAML object | 解析失败：SKILL.md is not a valid YAML object |
| Frontmatter has no `name` | 解析失败：SKILL.md is missing "name" |
| `version` is not three numeric parts x.y.z | version 不合法 |
| Slug already taken | slug 已被占用，换一个 |
| Submitted package is empty | 空文件 |
docs_page.publish_package_version_note: On first creation a missing `version` in the frontmatter is treated as 1.0.0 and is not rejected. When publishing a new version, `version` is mandatory.
docs_page.publish_visibility_table:
| Level | What other logged-in users see | Files and downloads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 公开 | Listed in browse, home, and search; description and files fully visible | Any logged-in user installs and downloads directly |
| 受限 | Still listed in browse and search; title, description, overview, and comments visible | The 「文件」, 「版本」, 「组合」, 「演练场」 tabs show a locked notice; manual download and `skills install` both require a request approved by you or by any administrator |
| 私密 | Absent from browse, home, and search; anyone else opening the detail page gets a 404, not a permission notice | Only you and administrators can view, download, and test it; editing the metadata stays author-only |
docs_page.publish_visibility_login: An anonymous visitor gets no files at any visibility level; manual download and `skills install` both demand a login first.
docs_page.publish_visibility_overview: 「受限」 locks the files only; the overview and the comment section stay open to everyone. Keep sensitive content out of the Overview.
docs_page.publish_visibility_bypass: The author and administrators bypass visibility entirely, drafts included.
docs_page.publish_visibility_labels: In the upload form and in the manage panel's 「编辑」 section the field is 「可见性 / 访问权限」, where 「受限」 is labelled 「受限下载」.
docs_page.publish_moderation_1: An administrator cannot delete a Skill. Only the author can: manage panel 「概览」 → 「危险操作」 → 「删除 Skill」. Deletion cannot be undone.
docs_page.publish_moderation_2: In the admin Skill list an administrator can change the status (草稿 / 已发布 / 已归档) and the visibility. Use 已归档 to unpublish.
docs_page.publish_moderation_3: Metadata such as the name, one-line description, Overview, and tags can be changed by the author only; an administrator who saves the edit form is refused.
docs_page.publish_moderation_4: A download request on a 「受限」 Skill can be decided by the author or by any administrator.
docs_page.publish_access_1: The requester sees the restricted notice where the install box would be, may enter a reason of up to 500 characters, and clicks 「申请下载」. When logged out the button reads 「登录后申请」.
docs_page.publish_access_2: After submission the page shows 「申请审核中…」. Re-submitting while pending or already approved is refused; after a rejection or a revocation you may apply again.
docs_page.publish_access_3: The author or an administrator handles them under 「访问申请」 in the manage panel; the pending count shows as a red badge on that tab. Decide each row with 「通过」 or 「拒绝」.
docs_page.publish_access_4: Approved users are listed under 「已授权用户」 on the same page; 「撤销」 takes the grant back. After a revocation that user no longer sees updates for this Skill in `skills update`.
docs_page.publish_access_5: Both the submitted request and the decision raise an in-app notification, plus a best-effort email according to the recipient's notification settings.
docs_page.publish_versions_1: Raise `version` inside the `SKILL.md` frontmatter first. The uploader has no version input, only the read-only line 「检测到版本：」.
docs_page.publish_versions_2: Open the 「Manage」 tab on the Skill detail page or the manage panel page, go to 「版本」 → 「上传新版本」, stage the complete new package, fill 「Changelog（可选）」 if needed, then click 「发布新版本」. The 「Manage」 tab appears for the author only; administrators use the manage panel page.
docs_page.publish_versions_3: The new version number must be strictly higher than every existing version, drafts and yanked versions included, so a yanked number can never be reused.
docs_page.publish_versions_4: Publishing makes the new version current and overwrites Token 成本 with the value estimated from the `SKILL.md` body, discarding any figure you typed. 「设为当前」 overwrites it the same way.
docs_page.publish_versions_table:
| Row action | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 设为当前 | That version becomes the one shown on the detail page and pulled by installs |
| 撤回 | Marks it 「已撤回」; yanking the current version falls back to the highest remaining published version, or clears the current version if there is none |
| 恢复 | Clears the 「已撤回」 mark |
docs_page.publish_subscribers_1: Publishing a version sends subscribers no notification. They find it through the version notice in the Workspace’s attention panel and Subscriptions list, or with `skills update` / `skills list` in the CLI.
docs_page.publish_subscribers_2: In the Workspace’s Subscriptions list, the old number in “v-old → v-new” is a snapshot taken when you clicked 「订阅更新」; updating through the CLI does not refresh it. Trust `skills list` for the version actually installed.
docs_page.publish_subscribers_3: A user without content access, including a restricted user whose grant was revoked, does not see this Skill in the update check at all.
docs_page.publish_remix_1: Click 「Remix」 on someone else's Skill detail page. It requires a login, a source Skill in published state, and content access to it; a restricted Skill without approval sends you back to the detail page.
docs_page.publish_remix_table:
| Remix copies | Remix does not copy |
| --- | --- |
| Name (with (Remix) appended), Slug (with -remix appended) | Every file in the package: scripts, assets, attachments |
| One-line description, Overview | Tags |
| The `SKILL.md` body | Triggers |
| Category, license, Token 成本 | Visibility and 来源分类 |
docs_page.publish_remix_2: Remixing a package that carries scripts or attachments leaves you with the body only; re-upload the scripts yourself.
docs_page.publish_remix_3: The new Skill always starts at 来源分类 「外部」, visibility 「公开」, and version 1.0.0. Change them afterwards in the edit form.
docs_page.publish_remix_4: The editor has a 「Diff vs 原版」 toggle showing added and removed line counts against the source. Submit with 「存为草稿」 or 「发布 Remix」. Afterwards the child page shows 「Fork 自」 the source, and the source page shows its Remix count.
docs_page.publish_packs_1: Packs are curated by administrators. A member cannot create one and there is no entry point for it in the interface.
docs_page.publish_packs_2: Switch to the 「合集包」 tab on the 「浏览 Skills」 page to see published packs, and open a pack page for its member list and install command.
docs_page.publish_packs_install_intro: One command installs every member of a pack:
docs_page.publish_packs_3: `install` takes multiple specs, so several `pack:` entries can be mixed with plain slugs and `slug@version`. A Skill is installed once only, and an explicit `@version` wins over the pack's entry.
docs_page.publish_packs_4: A pack only ever contains installable Skills: published, not deleted, not private. A pack only ever contains installable Skills: published, not deleted, not private.
docs_page.publish_packs_5: A restricted Skill can be a pack member, but you must get your request approved on its own page first; otherwise that one entry fails and the remaining members still install.
docs_page.publish_packs_6: Once a member is archived, made private, or deleted, it disappears from the pack page and the install manifest with no notice to anyone. A pack with no installable member shows no install command, only 「这个合集包还没有可安装的 skill。」
docs_page.disc_intro: The discussion area lives at /discussion and has two tabs, “Posts” and “Topics”. Reading is open to everyone; publishing, commenting, reacting and +1 require a sign-in.
docs_page.disc_entry_nav: Open it from “Discussion” in the nav bar; it lands on the “Posts” tab.
docs_page.disc_entry_post: Post an update: on the “Posts” tab click the box reading “Share an idea, an update or a resource…”, write the body, add attachments, then click “Publish”. The card is prepended to the feed without navigating away.
docs_page.disc_entry_topic: Start a topic: switch to the “Topics” tab first, then click “Start a discussion” at the top right. That button only renders on the “Topics” tab — there is no entry point from the feed.
docs_page.disc_entry_anon: Any write action while signed out redirects to the sign-in page and returns you to the same page afterwards.
docs_page.disc_pick_rule: Use a post for one line, one image, one shared resource. Use a topic for a question that needs a title, categories and a thread that stays findable. The two are separate; published content cannot be converted from one into the other.
docs_page.disc_pick_table:
| Item | Post | Topic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | none | required, 4–120 characters |
| Categories | none | 1–3 required |
| Body limit | 8,000 characters | 20,000 characters, may be empty |
| Engagement | 6 reaction types + 2-level comments | +1 + 2-level replies |
| View count | not tracked | shown on the topic page |
| Editable after publishing | body only | title, body, categories, attachments |
docs_page.disc_topics_p1: A topic takes 1–3 categories, picked in the “Choose topics (multiple allowed, up to 3)” dropdown. A fourth pick shows “Pick at most 3 topics”; none shows “Pick at least one topic”. Posts have no categories.
docs_page.disc_topics_list:
- Tech talk
- Models & algorithms
- Agents & tools
- Skill development
- Research
- Q&A
- Sharing
- Showcase
docs_page.disc_topics_legacy: Older topics may still show “General”. That category is retired and cannot be picked. Editing such a topic starts with no category and shows “The original category was retired — please pick a topic again”; pick 1–3 before saving.
docs_page.disc_sort_feed: Feed sorting: “Newest” (default) and “Hot”. “Hot” orders by engagement and the order shifts as people react, so paging can repeat or skip posts; use “Newest” for a stable order.
docs_page.disc_sort_forum: Topic sorting: “Latest reply”, “Top”, “Newest”. The “Categories” sidebar filters by category; “All topics” clears the filter.
docs_page.disc_sort_pinned: Pinned content always sits above the chosen sort.
docs_page.disc_sort_counts: Sidebar counts count a topic once per category, so a topic with 3 categories is counted three times and the per-category numbers add up to more than “All topics”.
docs_page.disc_sort_search: Search works on both tabs: on “Posts” it matches body text only, returns at most the latest 20 hits and has no paging; on “Topics” it matches title and body and pages normally. Clicking any category clears the search box.
docs_page.disc_attach_table:
| Kind | Count cap | Size cap each | Formats |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Images | 9 | 10 MB | JPEG / PNG / WebP / AVIF / GIF |
| Uploaded video | 1 | 1 GB | MP4 / WebM / MOV |
| External video link | 1, mutually exclusive with an uploaded video | — | full http / https URL |
| File attachments | 4 | 100 MB | Any format (source code, JSON, CSV, Markdown, archives, Office, PDF…) |
| Total per post or topic | 14 | — | — |
docs_page.disc_attach_quota: Video and document uploads count against a per-account budget of 5 GB per rolling 24 hours; images do not count. Over the cap the upload fails with “daily upload quota reached”. The budget is charged the moment an upload finishes, even if you never click “Publish”, and is not refunded.
docs_page.disc_attach_link: An external video link renders as a link card showing “External video, opens in a new tab”, with no preview image — the intranet blocks embedded players. An incomplete address shows “Enter a full video URL (including https://)”; anything that is not http/https shows “Only http/https links are supported”.
docs_page.disc_attach_reuse: An uploaded file can be attached to one post or topic only. Reusing an attachment URL from somewhere else is rejected with “That attachment is already used by other content — please upload it again.” Upload a second copy; it is charged to the 5 GB budget again.
docs_page.disc_attach_frozen: A post’s attachments are frozen once published — “Edit” changes the body only, and the body cannot be emptied. A topic’s attachments can be replaced wholesale in “Edit”.
docs_page.disc_attach_login: Uploaded videos and documents require a sign-in to open and are unreachable for signed-out visitors; images inside the body are served publicly.
docs_page.disc_attach_open: Clicking an attachment card opens it in the in-page preview drawer: images, videos, audio and PDFs are shown directly (PDF through the browser’s own viewer), source code and text get syntax highlighting, JSON is pretty-printed, CSV renders as a table and Markdown toggles between rendered and source (large files show their first 1 MB); HTML, SVG and XML are shown as source only. Formats that cannot be previewed — archives, executables, Office documents — are marked “Download only” on the card and open to a “no preview” card with a download button; executables and scripts carry a caution line. The download icon on the right of a card downloads without opening the preview. Attachment cards have no thumbnail and videos have no poster frame.
docs_page.disc_attach_pending: While an upload is in flight “Publish” and “Save” stay disabled with progress shown on the button, and adding a link shows “Wait for the current upload to finish”. Formats such as .mkv and .avi are rejected.
docs_page.disc_limits_table:
| Field | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Post body | 8,000 characters; body and attachments cannot both be empty |
| Topic title | 4–120 characters, required |
| Topic body | 20,000 characters, may be empty |
| Post comment | 1–2,000 characters |
| Topic reply | 1–5,000 characters |
docs_page.disc_comments_levels: Two levels only. Replying to a reply still attaches to that thread root — there is no third level — and the person you answered is still notified.
docs_page.disc_comments_delete_replies: Deleting a comment that already has replies turns it into a “This comment was deleted” placeholder and keeps every reply under it; once the last reply is deleted the placeholder disappears on its own. Replies behave the same and show “This reply was deleted”.
docs_page.disc_comments_delete_leaf: A comment with no replies is removed outright, leaving no placeholder. A confirmation asks “Delete this comment?” or “Delete this reply?” first.
docs_page.disc_comments_noedit: Comments and replies cannot be edited after posting, only deleted — by their author or by an admin.
docs_page.disc_comments_paging: A post page shows 3 threads first; “Load more comments” adds 10 at a time. Each thread previews 2 replies; “Show … more replies” loads the rest, capped at 200.
docs_page.disc_comments_topic_paging: Topic replies have no paging: at most 300 root replies render, each with at most 100 nested replies; anything beyond that is not shown.
docs_page.disc_comments_sort: A “Most relevant” / “Most recent” switch appears once there is more than one thread. Post comments can be liked; topic replies cannot.
docs_page.disc_comments_notify: You get an in-app notification when someone comments on your post or topic, or replies to your comment; clicking it jumps to that entry and highlights it. Email is off by default — turn it on under “Settings” → “Notifications”. Reactions and +1 send no notification.
docs_page.disc_react_list:
- Like
- Celebrate
- Support
- Love
- Insightful
- Curious
docs_page.disc_react_open: Hover “Like” for about 0.35 s to open the palette of 6 reactions. A plain click means “Like”; if your current reaction is another type, a plain click removes it.
docs_page.disc_react_switch: One reaction per person per post: clicking the same type again removes it, clicking another switches in place.
docs_page.disc_react_count: The count is the total across all reaction types, so switching type never changes the number; only adding or removing does.
docs_page.disc_react_panel: Click the stats row to open the “Reactions” panel, filterable by type, 30 people per page; signed out it shows “Sign in to view”.

docs_page.klib_intro: The library lives at `/library`. Submit a web article, PDF, EPUB, HTML, PPTX or DOCX; once it is parsed into chapters you can read it online, highlight it, annotate it and ask the AI about it.
docs_page.klib_submit_p1: Open 「知识库」 in the top nav and click 「添加内容」 at the top right. Without a session you get the toast 「请先登录再添加内容」 and are sent to the login page. The dialog has two tabs: 「链接」 for a URL, 「文件」 for a local document. There is no size cap on uploads.
docs_page.klib_submit_inputs_table:
| Input | Tab | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web link | 「链接」 | http(s) web articles only; URL up to 2048 characters; 30 s fetch timeout, at most 5 redirects; extraction fails below 200 characters of readable text; at most 24 images re-hosted, each up to 8 MB |
| PDF | 「文件」 | Scanned PDFs and PDFs with broken embedded font encodings carry no text layer |
| EPUB | 「文件」 | — |
| PPTX, DOCX | 「文件」 | — |
| HTML, HTM | 「文件」 | 「下载原文件」 returns the source as plain text, unrendered |
docs_page.klib_submit_p2: A link pointing at a PDF is rejected: download the file and import it from the 「文件」 tab. Links to images, audio, video and archives are rejected as well.
docs_page.klib_submit_p3: 「类型」 defaults to 「自动识别」; the options are 书籍 / 论文 / 博客 / 文章 / 报告 / 其他. 「主题分类（可多选，留空由 AI 识别）」 accepts at most 4. A type or category you pick by hand is never changed by the AI afterwards; the AI only fills what you leave empty.
docs_page.klib_submit_p4: If the URL or the file content already exists in the library you get 「该内容已在知识库中」 and land on the existing document: no new entry is created, the type and categories you picked are discarded, and you are not its uploader, so you cannot edit it.
docs_page.klib_submit_limits: Per user, per hour: 20 link submissions, 10 file uploads, 6 re-parses, 6 AI digest generations. Beyond that you get 「操作过于频繁，请稍后再试」.
docs_page.klib_processing_p1: Submitting holds the page until parsing finishes, so the document is usually readable by the time its detail page opens; a large PDF or EPUB just makes that wait longer. A document becomes readable only once parsing has finished. A document becomes readable only once parsing has finished.
docs_page.klib_processing_table:
| Badge | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 处理中 | Text and table of contents not built yet; the panel shows 「正在提取内容…」 | Wait; the panel polls every 3 s and refreshes itself when done |
| 处理失败 | Parsing failed; the panel shows the raw error | The uploader or an admin clicks 「重试」 |
| No badge | Ready | 「开始阅读」 appears in the left column, or 「继续阅读」 once you have progress |
docs_page.klib_processing_p2: A scanned PDF yields a single notice chapter and no text layer: the table of contents holds only that notice, the AI digest fails with 「无可分析文本」, chat returns 「该文档没有可分析的文本」, and highlights cannot anchor. The original file still pages through normally.
docs_page.klib_read_login: Reading requires a session, 公开 documents included. Logged out, the detail page shows 「申请阅读」; clicking it only sends you to the login page, and after logging in you land on the home page rather than back on the document. Log in first, then open the library.
docs_page.klib_read_pdf: A PDF is shown by the built-in renderer with the original page layout; there is no view switch. Bottom right: page-number box, zoom minus / plus (0.4x to 3x) and 「适应宽度」.
docs_page.klib_read_layout: For non-PDF documents, the toolbar 「Aa」 switches between 「连续滚动」 and 「分章阅读」 and sets font size (15 to 24), typeface, line height, column width and theme; these settings stay in the current browser only. Above 400,000 extracted characters 「连续滚动」 is unavailable and shows 「该文档篇幅较长，暂不支持连续滚动」.
docs_page.klib_read_toc: The toolbar 「目录」 lists every chapter with an AI summary of at most 120 characters; clicking jumps there, and in a PDF it jumps to the chapter's page range. Left and right arrow keys move between chapters, Esc closes the topmost panel. Reading progress is saved automatically on a 5 s interval.
docs_page.klib_marks_highlight: Select text in the reading column and the floating toolbar shows 4 colour dots (yellow, green, blue, pink); click one to create a highlight. A highlight stores at most 300 characters and keeps only the beginning beyond that; you get at most 500 highlights per document, then 「这篇文档的高亮已达上限」. Clicking an existing highlight lets you recolour it, write a note or delete it.
docs_page.klib_marks_note: Select text and click the sticky-note icon 「笔记」: a yellow highlight is created and the 「笔记」 panel opens with the cursor in that entry's box (placeholder 「写点想法…」), up to 1000 characters. Click 「保存」 to commit.
docs_page.klib_marks_selection: The same floating toolbar also carries 「复制」, 「翻译」 and 「问 AI」; 「问 AI」 drops the selected sentence into the AI panel's input.
docs_page.klib_translate_p1: Select text and click 「翻译」. The direction is decided automatically: Chinese goes to English, anything else goes to Simplified Chinese. Up to 3000 characters per call, 60 calls per hour per user.
docs_page.klib_shared_p1: Turn on 「公开我的笔记」 at the top of the 「笔记」 panel. The scope is the whole document and it applies retroactively: every highlight and note text you have on this document becomes visible to other logged-in users who have read access to it. There is no per-highlight switch.
docs_page.klib_shared_p2: Turn the switch off and those marks go private again; nobody can post new replies to them.
docs_page.klib_shared_p3: Other people's marks appear as dotted underlines with a margin badge 「N 人在此批注」; clicking it opens the 「笔记」 panel on that note. The 「显示他人标注」 switch is on by default and is remembered per browser; per author there are 「只看」 and an eye icon (hide / show again), remembered per document. When community marks seem to be gone, check those two first — the panel says they are hidden by a filter and tells you to click 「全部显示」.
docs_page.klib_shared_p4: Click 「回复」 on someone's public note, up to 4000 characters; the note's author is notified. Once the author switches sharing off, new replies are refused.
docs_page.klib_ai_p1: Click the sparkle icon 「问问 AI」 in the toolbar to open 「问问这篇文档」. If the AI has never read the document, click 「生成 AI 导读」 first: any logged-in user can trigger it, the result is shared by everyone, regenerating overwrites the digest everyone sees, and the cap is 6 per hour per user. While it runs the panel shows 「AI 正在阅读本文档…」.
docs_page.klib_ai_p2: Once ready the panel offers suggested-question chips. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a newline, a message is capped at 4000 characters, and the limit is 60 per hour per user. The eraser icon is 「清空对话」. Conversations are kept per user per document.
docs_page.klib_ai_cite: Citations in an answer are circled-number superscripts. Click one and the reading column scrolls to the cited passage and flashes it; in a PDF it jumps to the matching page; in 「分章阅读」 it switches to that chapter first, then locates the passage.

| Visibility | Wording on the page | Who can read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 公开 | 所有登录用户可见、可阅读 | Any logged-in user |
| 受限 | 所有人可见简介，阅读需要你的批准 | The uploader, admins, and approved requesters |

docs_page.klib_access_p1: On a 受限 document click 「申请阅读」, optionally fill 「说明申请理由（可选）」 with up to 500 characters, click 「提交申请」, and the state becomes 「申请审批中」. The uploader decides; admins can act too. The decision list is inline on the detail page under 「阅读申请」 with 「通过」, 「拒绝」 and 「撤销」. After a rejection you can click 「重新申请阅读」. Limit: 20 requests per hour per user.
docs_page.klib_access_p2: Browse lists and search exclude 私密 documents and any document that has not finished processing.
docs_page.klib_edit_p1: The uploader and admins click 「编辑内容与信息」 on the detail page, or go straight to `/library/'<slug>'/edit`. Covers accept JPG / PNG / WebP up to 10 MB.
docs_page.klib_edit_pin: Fields you edit by hand are pinned: once you save 「标题」, 「作者」 or 「简介」, a re-fetch or re-parse will not overwrite them; once you save 「类型」 or 「分类」, the AI never changes them again. 「摘要」 is yours to write, up to 20000 characters, and is touched by neither extraction nor AI.
docs_page.klib_edit_reprocess: 「重新解析」 overwrites the extracted content, including chapter text you edited by hand; the confirmation dialog says so. For a link-based document it re-fetches the live page: if the source changed or died, the document can end up 处理失败 with the old content already gone. After a re-parse, a highlight sitting on repeated text can re-anchor to a different occurrence.
docs_page.klib_categories_p1: Categories are a fixed set, not free tags; at most 4 per document, beyond which you get 「最多选择 4 个分类」. Left empty, the AI fills them in once.
docs_page.klib_categories_list: 教程 · 开发实践 · Agent · 大模型 · 提示工程 · RAG · 多模态 · 训练微调 · 推理部署 · 数据工程 · 评测 · 安全对齐 · 具身智能 · 产品设计 · 行业观察 · 学术前沿
docs_page.klib_types_p1: 「类型」 and topic categories are two independent facets. 「类型」 and topic categories are two independent facets: 「类型」 is single-choice, categories are multi-select.
docs_page.klib_shelf_p1: Click 「加入书架」 on a detail page to shelve the document; the button becomes 「已在书架」. The entry point is 「我的书架」 in the user menu, at `/library/shelf`. The shelf holds only what you add by hand — it is not an automatic recently-read list.
docs_page.klib_shelf_p2: Three counters sit at the top of the shelf: 全部, 在读, 已读完 — a document counts as 已读完 at 98% progress. Sort by 「最近阅读」 or 「最近加入」, filter by type; at most 200 rows are shown.
docs_page.evt_intro: “Events” is the community event calendar — academic conferences, internal events, expert talks and seminars all go here. Any logged-in member can publish an event. Lists and detail pages are visible to visitors who are not logged in; the meeting link is the only exception.
docs_page.evt_publish_who: Open “Events” (`/events`) in the navbar and click “Publish an event” at the top right. If you are not logged in you go through the login page first and come back to the form.
docs_page.evt_publish_steps:
1. Fill in “Event title” (required) and “One-line summary” (optional, shown on the event card).
2. Pick “Event type” — one of the four cards, required.
3. Pick “Topics” — optional, up to 3.
4. Fill in “Time”: for an all-day or multi-day event tick “All-day or multi-day event (like a conference — shown by date only)”; otherwise enter the start date and time and confirm the event time zone below.
5. Pick “Format”, then fill in the meeting link or the location and city it asks for; for external events also fill in “Website or registration link”.
6. Under “Cover image” click “Upload cover” (optional); use “About this event” for the agenda, speaker background and how to join (optional).
7. To list speakers, tick “Add speakers and guests” and fill in one block per person.
8. Click “Publish event”. You land on the event detail page.
docs_page.evt_publish_rate: Each account may publish at most 10 events per hour; further attempts are rejected until an hour has passed.
docs_page.evt_facets_note: “Event type” and “Topics” are two independent axes. The type describes the format of the gathering: required, exactly one value. Topics describe the subject matter: optional, several allowed. In the filter rail they apply separately.

docs_page.evt_topics_p: Topics are a fixed set of 10: Agents & tools, Large models, Multimodal, Graphics & vision, Algorithms, Embodied AI, Compute & systems, Data engineering, Frontier research, Other.
docs_page.evt_topics_cap: Up to 3 topics per event; Up to 3 topics per event; a fourth click is refused with “Pick at most 3 topics”. An event publishes with no topic at all.. An event publishes with no topic at all.
docs_page.evt_time_tz_p: Enter start and end times in the event time zone you selected — what you type is the wall-clock time in that zone. There are four zones, defaulting to Eastern Time (Toronto). No other zone is available: for an event in London or Tokyo, convert the times into one of these four zones before entering them.
docs_page.evt_tz_table:

|---|---|
| Eastern Time (Toronto) | Eastern |
| Mountain Time (Edmonton) | Mountain |
| Pacific Time (Vancouver) | Pacific |
| Beijing Time | Beijing |
docs_page.evt_time_viewer: Every member sees the time converted into their own browser time zone; when that differs from the event zone, the card and the detail page also show the event-zone time on a second line. Right after the page opens it shows the event zone, then switches to your local zone — that is expected.
docs_page.evt_time_allday: Tick “All-day or multi-day event” and you fill in dates only, no times, and the time-zone select disappears. All-day events are never converted: every member sees the same date.
docs_page.evt_time_rules_list:
- For a timed event the end time must be later than the start time.
- An end date different from the start date with no end time is refused: add the end time or tick “all-day”.
- For an all-day event the end date cannot be earlier than the start date; the same date means a single-day event.
- The start year must fall between 2000 and 2100.
- “Upcoming” is judged in the event’s own zone: an event moves to “Past events” only after its last day has ended in that zone.
docs_page.evt_mode_table:
| Format | What to fill in | Shown on the card |
|---|---|---|
| Online | Meeting link | Online event |
| In person | Location, city | Location · city |
| Hybrid | Meeting link, location, city | Location · city |
docs_page.evt_mode_wipe: Saving clears whatever the current format hides: switching to “Online” drops the location and city, switching to “In person” drops the meeting link. Do not toggle the format back and forth just to look at the other fields.
docs_page.evt_city_p: The city list is fixed: Vancouver, Toronto, Edmonton, Montreal, Waterloo, Ottawa, China. The city is optional, but no other value can be typed in — put the exact address in the location field.
docs_page.evt_meeting_p: The meeting link is visible to logged-in members only — visitors who are not logged in see “Log in to see the meeting link”, and the link never reaches the page. It is also left out of the “Download .ics” file and the Google Calendar link, so attendees have to come back to the event page and click “Join online meeting”. “Website / registration”, speaker details and the location carry no such restriction; anonymous visitors see them.
docs_page.evt_calendar_p: The time card on the detail page offers two entries: “Google Calendar” opens a pre-filled Google Calendar draft in a new tab; “Download .ics” downloads a calendar file for any calendar client. Both carry absolute instants, which the recipient’s calendar converts to local time; all-day events are written as plain dates.
docs_page.evt_calendar_note: A timed event with no end time is exported as 1 hour. The entry description contains only the one-line summary and the link to the event page. Once an event is cancelled, exported titles are prefixed with [Cancelled].
docs_page.evt_speakers_p: Ticking “Add speakers and guests” adds one blank speaker block; “Add another speaker” adds more, “Upload photo” attaches a portrait. Only the name is required.

docs_page.evt_speakers_warn: Editing an event replaces the whole speaker list: after saving, the event has exactly the speakers present in the form. Before changing any field, check that every speaker is still listed; unticking “Add speakers and guests” and saving removes all of them.
docs_page.evt_manage_p: All management actions sit in the “Manage event” box on the event detail page: “Edit”, “Cancel event” / “Restore event”, “Feature” / “Unfeature”, “Delete”. Only the author can change event content — an admin opening the edit page gets a 404 and can only cancel, feature and delete.

docs_page.evt_cancel_p: Cancelling is not deleting. A cancelled event stays in the lists and the calendar with a red “Cancelled” badge, a struck-through title, the notice “This event has been cancelled” on the detail page, and a [Cancelled] prefix in calendar exports. “Restore event” undoes it. Cancelled events drop out of “Featured events”.
docs_page.evt_delete_p: Deleting removes the event from every list, the calendar and search, and there is no restore anywhere in the UI. If the event is simply not happening, use “Cancel event” instead.
docs_page.evt_pin_p: Featuring is admin-only and capped at 3 events at a time; once 3 are featured, a further attempt is rejected until you unfeature one. The “Featured events” strip shows only featured events that have not ended and have not been cancelled.

docs_page.evt_limits_note: Cover images and speaker photos accept JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and GIF; a non-image file is refused with “Please choose an image file”, and while an upload is running the submit button reads “Uploading image…” and stays disabled. Links are not format-checked: a link with no scheme is opened as `http://`, and a wrong address only surfaces when someone clicks it.
docs_page.evt_browse_p: The list splits into “Upcoming” and “Past events”. The left filter rail (Date, Type, Topic, Format, City) and the mini calendar appear on wide screens only; on a phone you get the event-type chips and the search box. Search matches the title, the one-line summary, the city and speaker names — not the “About this event” body, so a keyword buried in the agenda will not be found. The list pages 30 events at a time; a multi-day event is dotted on every day of the calendar but appears once in the list.
docs_page.evt_videos_p1: The video board lives at `/videos`. The navbar entry reads “Geek Hub”; the page itself is titled “Geek Videos”. The whole board requires login — visitors who are not logged in see nothing.
docs_page.evt_videos_p2: Videos are curated: only admins upload and publish them. Members have no upload entry and cannot publish a video. Route content you want on the board through an admin.
docs_page.evt_videos_p3: As a logged-in member you can watch; click “Like”; click “Save” to keep the video in your own list; click “Share” to copy the link; post comments and replies; and use “AI Summary” and “Ask about this video” in the side panel. The list supports search, category filtering and “Latest” / “Trending” / “Most viewed” sorting.
docs_page.evt_videos_p4: Drafts and private videos are visible only to the uploader and admins. An “Unlisted” video is kept out of the lists, but any logged-in member holding the link can watch it — do not use unlisted as access control.
docs_page.acct_intro: Click your avatar in the top right and choose “Settings”. The page is titled “Account settings” and has eight tabs in the left sidebar. Your profile and your workspace are reached from “Profile” in the same avatar menu.

docs_page.acct_profile_editable: Editable fields: display name (2–64 characters), headline (60 characters max), bio (240 characters max, anything longer is cut), About me (rich text, 4,000 characters max), interests (up to 12, 20 characters each), links (up to 6, http / https addresses only), profile banner and avatar. Press “Save” when done. “View profile”, next to the page title, opens your profile.
docs_page.acct_profile_avatar: Use “Upload avatar” to pick a file and the trash button next to it to clear it. Formats: JPG / PNG / WebP / AVIF / GIF, 10MB per file. Except for GIFs, avatars and profile banners are re-encoded in your browser as WebP or JPEG (at most 2048 px on the long edge) before upload: location, device model and other embedded metadata never leave your device, and the photo’s orientation is applied to the image itself. A GIF keeps its original file so the animation still plays. A successful upload still requires “Save” to take effect — leave the page without saving and the avatar is lost.
docs_page.acct_profile_readonly: Email, employee ID, sign-in method and W3 name are read-only; the interface offers no way to change them. On an email/password account the “Employee ID” field shows the local part of your email address.
docs_page.acct_private_where: The first switch on the Privacy tab is “Private account”, off by default. It saves immediately; the “Profile sections” card on the same tab needs its Save button.

| Hidden from other members once on | Still public |
|---|---|

| The @handle next to your name and on your card | Your card’s style, photo or video, and your badges |

| Your email, @handle and employee ID on download requests you send (the author sees only your display name plus a “Private account” marker) | Every profile section you have not turned off, and the profile link itself |
docs_page.acct_private_admins: Administrators always see everything, and see a “Private account” marker on your profile (「隐私账号」 in the Chinese-only admin console at `/manage/users`). Your profile link keeps working — a private account does not hide the page itself.
docs_page.acct_sections_where: Adjust them in the “Profile sections” card under Settings → Privacy: reorder the 11 sections with ↑↓ or by dragging, flip each section’s public switch, then press Save; “Reset” restores the default order with everything shown. A section you turn off is visible only to you and to administrators holding the identity permission, marked “Only visible to you”. Everyone else loses the tab, and its numbers are left out of the profile stats and your card. The card’s “Preview as a visitor” link lets you check the result. Switches turned off before September 2026 were carried over; if “Posts & forum topics” was off, both the Posts and Topics sections stay hidden.

| Shelf | Everyone; public documents only |
docs_page.acct_sections_docs_note: The profile’s Documents section lists only ready, non-private library documents — for you too. Processing, failed and private documents are in your Workspace.
docs_page.acct_reading_toggle: “Show my reading activity” is on by default: documents you add to your shelf list your name in the “Currently reading” roster on their detail page. Turn it off and you are counted but not named.
docs_page.acct_reading_notes: This switch does not cover reading notes. Note sharing is a separate, per-document switch inside the reader: if you shared notes on a document, you stay in that document's “Readers sharing annotations” list even with this switch off.
docs_page.acct_pvd_intro: The Workspace is the last tab of your profile. Only you can see it, and it replaces the old “Dashboard”. The section tabs are what others see; the Workspace is what you work from:
docs_page.acct_pvd_table:
| | Profile section tabs | Workspace |
|---|---|---|
| Who can see it | Set in “Profile sections”: sections you did not hide are public; Videos, Zones and Votes are for signed-in members only | Only you — it is hidden in visitor view too |
| Skills | Published, non-private ones | All of them, including drafts, archived and private, with status, version, pending download requests and a “Manage” link |
| Library documents | Ready, non-private ones | All of them, including processing, failed and private, with an “Edit” link and pending read requests |
| Drafts | Not shown | “Drafts”: Skill drafts, zone post drafts and vote drafts, most recently edited first |
| Needs your attention | Not shown | Download requests, read requests, submissions waiting for review in votes that have not ended, and subscriptions with a new version — each linked to where you handle it |

| Favorites | Not shown | Your most recently favorited Skills |
| Events | Events you created | Events you joined, upcoming first |
