docs_page.acct_dept_source: Department and lab come from the company employee directory, matched by employee ID at every login. You cannot edit them. Check the current values in the “Current department / lab” card on the Privacy tab; if they are wrong, contact an administrator.
docs_page.acct_dept_no_w3: Matching uses the W3 employee ID only. An account that has only ever logged in with email and password has no employee ID to match, so the card keeps showing “None (no employee-directory entry matches your employee ID)”. Log in once via W3 to get matched.
docs_page.acct_dept_overwrite: The roster is the only source: once an administrator changes or blanks the department / institute there, your next login overwrites the values on the site — including clearing them. Deactivated roster entries are excluded from all syncing.
docs_page.acct_notif_where: The switches are on the Notifications tab, laid out as one table with the columns “Type” / “In-app” / “Email”. They do not auto-save: press “Save”, or leaving the page discards your changes.
docs_page.acct_notif_table:
| Type | When it fires | In-app default | Email default |
|---|---|---|---|
| Comments / replies | Someone replies to your comment or reply: videos, feedback board, discussion posts, forum topics, library comments and reading notes | On | Off |
| Access requests received | Someone requests download access to a restricted skill you published, or read access to a restricted document you submitted | On | On |
| Request decisions | Your request is approved, rejected or revoked | On | On |
| Announcements | An administrator publishes a platform announcement | On | Off |
docs_page.acct_notif_bell: In-app notifications live only in the bell dropdown in the navbar. There is no separate notifications page and no paging: the panel lists the 20 most recent items, and anything older cannot be retrieved through the interface. The unread badge caps at 99+. “Mark all read” clears the unread marks; an empty panel shows “No notifications yet”. Clicking an item opens the target in a new tab — with a popup blocker nothing appears to happen, but the item is marked read. Announcements are the exception: they remain browsable at `/announcements`.
docs_page.acct_notif_limits: Your own actions never notify you. Library comment replies, reading-note replies and library access notifications are in-app only — they send no email, whatever the “Email” column says.
docs_page.acct_security_table:
| Sign-in method | What the Security tab offers |
|---|---|
| Email & password | The “Change password” form; your current password is required |
| W3 | No site password to change; the tab shows only “W3 account: authentication is managed by the company — no local password.” |
| Email & password + W3 | The “Change password” form; both sign-in methods stay available |
docs_page.acct_security_password: A new password is 8 to 128 characters and must be entered identically twice. If you already have one, “Current password” must be correct first; a wrong value returns “Current password is incorrect”.
docs_page.acct_security_both: A W3-only account cannot set a site password, so it cannot log in while corporate authentication is unavailable. The reverse works: an account that already has a password and logs in once via W3 with the same email keeps both methods and can still change the password.
docs_page.acct_lang_where: The Language tab offers three choices: 中文, English, Français. The change takes effect immediately; there is nothing to save.
docs_page.acct_lang_cookie: The choice is stored in a cookie in the current browser for one year; it is not tied to your account. On another browser or device, or after clearing cookies, the language falls back to your browser preference: `en*` gives English, `fr*` gives French, anything else gives Chinese.
docs_page.conduct_intro: This code applies to everything members publish here: Skills, library documents, discussion posts and forum topics, events, feedback, and all comments and replies on them. Publishing content here means you accept this code.
docs_page.conduct_d_1: Post in the right place. A forum topic must carry 1 to 3 subjects; if the subjects do not match the body, an administrator changes them or deletes the topic.
docs_page.conduct_d_2: Review the content, not the person. Point to a precise location (file, chapter, reproduction steps) and a verifiable conclusion. Do not judge the author’s ability, rank, or motives.
docs_page.conduct_d_3: No harassment, personal attacks, insults, or labelling. No discriminatory remarks about ethnicity, region, gender, age, religion, or health.
docs_page.conduct_d_4: No pornographic or sexually explicit material, in body text, images, video, or attachments.
docs_page.conduct_d_5: Do not publish someone else’s private information: phone numbers, home addresses, private chat screenshots, photos taken without consent. When a member has turned on 「Private account」, do not fill in their department or lab in your text or comments.
docs_page.conduct_d_6: Do not end an argument by deleting the thread. Deleting your own post or topic also removes every comment and reply other people wrote on it, with no way to restore them.
docs_page.conduct_d_7: No flooding. Each account is limited to 10 posts, 10 forum topics, and 10 feedback items per hour, and 10 comments or replies per minute. Requests beyond that are rejected.
docs_page.conduct_a_1: Publish only what you have the right to publish. When you quote or rework someone else’s Skill, document, or code, name the source and the original author in the body.
docs_page.conduct_a_2: To modify someone else’s Skill, use 「Remix」 on its detail page. The new Skill must use a different name and slug, must state in its body which Skill it derives from (for example “based on pdf-form-signer”), and must keep the original `license` field. If that licence requires attribution, comply with it.
docs_page.conduct_a_3: Do not re-upload someone else’s Skill as your own work, and do not use a lookalike name to pass yours off as the original.
docs_page.conduct_a_4: Do not impersonate anyone. One account per person; never publish under another person’s name, employee ID, or department.
docs_page.conduct_a_5: Never mark material that must not circulate as public. Use 「Restricted download」 and approve each 「Request download」 individually. For a public Skill, file names and sizes are visible without logging in — only the file contents require a login — so keep sensitive wording out of file names too.
docs_page.conduct_p_1: No advertising, promotion, group recruiting, job postings, or contract-work solicitation, including funnel links buried in body text or comments.
docs_page.conduct_p_2: No automated scraping. Do not crawl pages or bulk-download content with scripts. Downloads count against your rolling 24-hour cap, so bulk pulls hit the ceiling immediately.
docs_page.conduct_p_3: A CLI token is an account credential. Use it only on your own machine; never commit it to shared scripts, repositories, group chats, or tickets. A token is shown once — if it leaks, go to `/settings/tokens`, hit 「Revoke」, and issue a new one.
docs_page.conduct_p_4: Do not share an account or its password, do not lend an account, and do not register more than one account for the same person.
docs_page.conduct_p_5: Do not work around visibility rules or quotas, whether by editing request parameters, sharing tokens, or switching accounts to download again.
docs_page.conduct_u_1: Attachments must be relevant to the content. One post or topic takes at most 9 images, 1 video, and 4 documents, capped at 14 attachments in total.
docs_page.conduct_u_2: A video may not exceed 1 GB, a document 100 MB, and video and document uploads count against a rolling 24-hour budget of 5 GB per account (body images do not count); past that, the upload fails.
docs_page.conduct_enforcement_intro: Administrators apply the following measures according to severity. Every administrator action on someone else’s content is written to the admin action log: time, administrator, action, target, details.
docs_page.conduct_enforcement_table:
| Measure | Effect |
|---|---|
| Content removal | Administrators can delete posts, forum topics, comments, replies, events, feedback, and library documents; a comment that already has replies is kept as a placeholder reading 「This comment was deleted」. |
| Lock and unpin | Administrators can lock a forum topic — the reply box is then replaced by 「An admin locked this topic — replies are closed」 — and can unpin anything at any time. |
| Skill withdrawal | Administrators can switch a Skill to 「Archived」 or to 「Private」, which removes it from browsing, search, and installation. Only the author can delete the Skill itself. |
| Lower download quota | Administrators adjust the per-account daily download cap (rolling 24 hours; blank means unlimited). Set to 0, the account cannot download at all — web and CLI requests are both refused. |
| CLI access revoked | Once CLI access is switched off, every CLI token of that account stops working immediately and the `skills` command is unusable. |
| Account deactivation | Once the account is disabled, it can no longer sign in with email and password, and its CLI tokens stop working. |
docs_page.conduct_e_1: Offending content is removed first. A repeat offender loses download quota or CLI access. Identity misuse, bulk scraping, and circulating unreleased material lead directly to account deactivation.
docs_page.conduct_e_2: Content that may contain unreleased material is removed first and verified afterwards.
docs_page.conduct_r_1: Content quality, platform defects, wrong visibility settings: open 「Feedback」 in the navigation bar, click 「Give feedback」 to open an item, and pick 「Bug report」 or 「Feature request」.
docs_page.conduct_r_2: Everything on that board is publicly visible. Do not put sensitive information, internal screenshots, or the names of the people involved into it.
docs_page.conduct_r_3: Harassment, personal attacks, leaked confidential material, a compromised account: contact a platform administrator directly instead of posting. There is no anonymous report form on the site, and a public post only spreads the material you are complaining about.
docs_page.conduct_r_4: To contest a measure, contact an administrator with your account, the content link, and the approximate time. Administrator actions are logged and can be checked.
docs_page.conduct_r_5: You can delete your own content and revoke your own tokens at any time. Content deleted by an administrator is not restored — library documents are the one exception and can be restored by an administrator.
docs_page.policy_intro: Set the visibility level before you submit, then confirm the content itself is allowed on this platform. These rules apply to Skills, library documents, the discussion board, events and videos alike.
docs_page.policy_levels_p1: Set a Skill's level under 「Visibility / access」 in the publish form and a library document's under 「Visibility」 in the submit form; both stay changeable from your own edit page. Events have no visibility switch — every event is visible to every visitor.
docs_page.policy_levels_table:
| Level | Title and summary | Body, files and reader |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Anyone who can reach this site, signed in or not | Any signed-in user |
| Restricted | Anyone who can reach this site, signed in or not | Approved case by case by the author or uploader: 「Request download」 on a Skill, 「Request access」 in the library |
| Private | You only (admins see it in the admin panel) | You only (admins see it in the admin panel) |
docs_page.policy_levels_note: 「Private」 content returns 404 to everyone else, so its existence is never revealed. Changing the level does not reach people who already downloaded — a downgrade cannot recall files that have left.
docs_page.policy_anon_p1: There is no site-wide login wall. Apart from Geek Hub (`/videos`, where the whole board requires login), list and detail pages are open to signed-out visitors; login only guards file bytes and the reader.
docs_page.policy_anon_table:
| Page | Signed-out visitor |
| --- | --- |
| Skill list, detail, 「Overview」, 「Reviews」 | Readable |
| The 「Files」 tab of a public Skill | File names and sizes readable; downloading bytes returns 401 |
| Library list, detail, summary | Readable; opening the reader redirects to login |
| Discussion posts, topics, comments and replies | Readable; attachment downloads and video playback return 401 |
| Event list, calendar, detail, speakers | Readable; 「Meeting link」 is stripped server-side and absent from the `.ics` |
| Feedback, packs, member profiles, search | Readable |
| Published announcements | Readable |
docs_page.policy_anon_note: Never rely on 「Public」 to protect anything: titles, summaries, author names and departments, and the full file list of a public Skill are all readable without logging in. Do not pick it when a file name itself is sensitive. Never rely on 「Public」 to protect anything, and do not pick it when a file name itself is sensitive.
docs_page.policy_anon_identity: Your display name and avatar are shown publicly alongside your content. Turn on 「Private account」 under Settings → 「Privacy」 to hide your department, lab and @handle; admins still see everything.
docs_page.policy_conf_p1: Upload only material within the classification level this platform is approved to hold. Anything above that level stays off the platform; if you are unsure of the level, confirm it with the owning function before submitting.
docs_page.policy_conf_1: No customer data: contracts, quotations, live-network logs, customer site information, tickets carrying a customer name.
docs_page.policy_conf_2: No personal data of third parties: another person's employee ID, phone number, email, home address, photo, performance or appraisal records.
docs_page.policy_conf_3: No credentials in Skill files, library documents, attachments or code blocks: account passwords, API keys, tokens, private keys, certificates, internal database connection strings.
docs_page.policy_conf_4: Use placeholders in every example config (`YOUR_API_KEY`, `example.com`), and search for key, secret, token and password before you submit.
docs_page.policy_conf_5: When in doubt pick 「Private」, then move to 「Restricted」 once a few people need it. 「Restricted」 guards only the body and the files — the title and summary stay visible to signed-out visitors, so keep sensitive wording out of titles.
docs_page.policy_third_1: Submit only documents and videos you have the right to share. Check the licence before reposting someone else's material, and keep the author credit.
docs_page.policy_third_2: When submitting a web page to the library, put the original address in 「Page URL」 instead of pasting the text in as a new document; 「View original source」 in the reader comes from that field.
docs_page.policy_third_3: When you Remix someone else's Skill, keep the original `license` field and the attribution. If that licence forbids redistribution or requires the same terms, follow it.
docs_page.policy_removal_p1: Admins can unpublish, hide or lock any content, and the action is recorded. The following are handled on sight:
docs_page.policy_removal_1: Library documents whose extraction failed, whose body is empty, or that duplicate an existing entry, plus repeat publications of the same Skill.
docs_page.policy_removal_2: Content filed under the wrong category or visibility to get around the rules — material that needs approval marked 「Public」, or 「Restricted」-grade content pasted into a discussion post.
docs_page.policy_removal_3: Content containing credentials, customer data or personal data of third parties.
docs_page.policy_removal_secret: Treat a credential as leaked the moment it is submitted: revoke and rotate it in the owning system first, then delete the content. Deleting is not sufficient — it may already have been downloaded or cached.
docs_page.policy_removal_report: There is no report button on this site. Contact an admin directly about a leaked credential or misclassified material. 「Feedback」 is a board anyone can read, so never post credentials, customer information or classified content there.
docs_page.policy_limits_p1: The following limits are enforced server-side; anything over is rejected outright.
docs_page.policy_limits_table:
| Item | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Post body | 8,000 characters |
| Topic title / body / topics | 4–120 chars / 20,000 chars / 1–3 |
| Topic reply | 5,000 characters |
| Post comment, feedback comment | 2,000 characters |
| Feedback title / body | 4–120 chars / 10,000 chars |
| Request reason, decision note | 500 characters |
| Attachments on one post or topic | ≤ 9 images, ≤ 1 video, ≤ 4 files, ≤ 14 total |
| Attachment file size | Video 1 GB; other files (any format) 100 MB |
| Inline editor image | 10 MB each |
| Upload traffic per user per day | 5 GB (rolling 24 hours), then uploads are refused until the next day |
| Upload rate | 6 attachments/minute; 30 inline images/minute |
| Pinned items | 5 posts, 3 events (admin action) |
| Library upload | No size cap; PDF / EPUB / HTML / PPTX / DOCX only |
docs_page.policy_limits_note: A video link takes the single video slot and must be an `http://` or `https://` address. A video or document already attached elsewhere cannot be reused on a second item — upload it again.
docs_page.desc_zones: Zones and roles, joining, post types and attachment previews, native embeds, wiki revisions and comment rules.
docs_page.zones_intro: Tech Zones live at /zones: self-governed zones organised by lab, department or technical direction, each with its own lead moderator, roles, members, posts and wiki. Everything under /zones requires a sign-in; signed-out visitors are sent to the login page first.
docs_page.zones_entry_nav: Open “Tech Zones” in the nav bar to reach the hub: featured zones, lab / department filters, the “All” and “My zones” tabs, and the latest posts across zones.
docs_page.zones_entry_hub: “My zones” lists the zones where you are the lead moderator or an active member. Members-only zones are still listed in the hub (name and tagline); their content opens only once you are a member.
docs_page.zones_entry_create: “Create zone” shows only for accounts granted “May create Tech Zones” (an admin turns it on under User management) and for admins holding the “Tech Zones” permission. The wizard has five steps: basics (name 2–40 characters, slug 3–40 lowercase letters / digits / dashes, tagline up to 80 characters) → organisation → access and joining → description and links (up to 8) → review.
docs_page.zones_entry_login: The creator becomes the lead moderator. Every new zone starts with three system roles: Moderator, Author and Member.
docs_page.zones_roles_p1: One role per person inside a zone. The lead moderator (the zone owner) implicitly holds every permission; everyone else gets exactly what their role grants, and a member without an assigned role is treated as the “Member” system role.
docs_page.zones_roles_table:
| Role | Default permissions | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lead moderator | all | the creator; nobody inside the zone can demote them — only “Transfer” |
| Moderator | Zone settings, Members, Publish, Moderate, Edit wiki, Comment | helps run the zone |
| Author | Publish, Edit wiki, Comment | may post and write wiki pages |
| Member | Comment | the default role; its permissions can be changed (e.g. grant Publish so everyone can post) but it cannot be deleted |
docs_page.zones_roles_perms_table:
| Permission | What it allows |
| --- | --- |
| Zone settings | edit name, description, cover / icon, organisation, links, visibility and join policy |
| Roles | create / edit / delete zone roles |
| Members | add / remove members, review join requests, assign roles, set member titles |
| Publish | publish articles, reports, papers, slides and links |
| Moderate | pin, lock, edit or delete any post or comment in the zone; publish announcements |
| Edit wiki | create, edit, move, delete wiki pages and restore revisions |
| Comment | comment and reply under posts |
docs_page.zones_roles_owner: Site admins holding the “Tech Zones” permission bypass zone visibility and every zone-level check and can moderate any zone — the backstop for governance; their actions are written to the admin log.
docs_page.zones_roles_custom: The lead moderator and anyone holding “Roles” can create up to 12 custom roles under “Zone settings → Roles”, tick any combination of permissions, rename or delete them; deleting a role drops its holders back to “Member”. System roles cannot be deleted and keep their keys.
docs_page.zones_roles_assign: “Members” cannot hand out a role that carries “Roles” unless the operator holds “Roles” too; the lead moderator’s own row cannot be edited on the members page.
docs_page.zones_roles_transfer: Transferring the lead moderator happens under “Zone settings → Danger zone” and only to an active member; the previous lead stays on as a Moderator. Site admins can also transfer by handle from “Manage → Tech Zones”.
docs_page.zones_join_visibility_table:
| Visibility | Who can read the content | Listed in the hub |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public | any signed-in user | yes |
| Members only | the lead moderator and active members | yes (name and tagline only) |
docs_page.zones_join_policy_table:
| Join policy | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Open | “Join” makes you a member immediately |
| Approval | a request (note up to 300 characters) goes to the pending list; a members manager approves or rejects it |
| Invite only | no join button — only a members manager can add you from the members page |
docs_page.zones_join_guest: A public zone can enable “Allow non-member comments”, letting any signed-in user comment under posts; off, only members may comment. Members-only zones are unaffected by this switch.
docs_page.zones_join_pending: Pending requests sit on the “Members → Pending” tab (with a count badge); until reviewed, the applicant sees “Requested” and clicking again does not submit a duplicate.
docs_page.zones_join_leave: Any member except the lead moderator can “Leave” at any time; the lead must transfer first. After being removed or rejected you may apply again.
docs_page.zones_join_notify: A join request notifies every members manager in-app (deep-linked to the pending tab); being added, approved, rejected, re-assigned, removed or made lead moderator notifies the person concerned. These notifications ignore the “Settings → Notifications” switches.
docs_page.zones_posts_compose: Publishing starts from the “Publish” button on the zone’s “Posts” tab. The editor is rich text (stored as Markdown) with images, stickers, polls and the “Embed” button (see below). Title 2–120 characters, summary up to 300, body up to 200,000.
docs_page.zones_posts_draft: A post saved as a draft is visible only to its author, co-authors and holders of “Moderate”; drafts are listed under “My drafts” in the zone’s right rail. The body is also auto-saved locally in the browser, so a refresh loses nothing.
docs_page.zones_posts_coauthors: Up to 12 co-authors, all of whom must be active members of the zone; co-authors can edit the post and appear in the author line.
docs_page.zones_posts_tags: Up to 8 tags of at most 24 characters each; clicking a tag filters the zone’s posts.
docs_page.zones_posts_cover: The cover image is uploaded as an image attachment and shown on list cards and at the top of the post page.
docs_page.zones_attach_preview_inline: Images, videos, audio and PDFs open in the in-page preview drawer (PDF through the browser’s own viewer). Source code and text are shown with syntax highlighting, JSON is pretty-printed, CSV renders as a table and Markdown toggles between rendered and source (large files show their first 1 MB). HTML, SVG and XML are shown as source only. Anything else gets a “no preview” card with a download button, and executables and scripts carry a caution line.
docs_page.zones_attach_preview_office: PPT / Word / Excel files are converted to a PDF preview on the server (LibreOffice) after upload: the attachment card shows “Converting” first, then “Preview available”. If conversion fails the download stays and the author or a moderator can click “Retry”.
docs_page.zones_attach_preview_slides: Without LibreOffice on the server, a PPTX still previews as HTML slides page by page (text plus images, simplified layout); DOCX previews by section the same way.
docs_page.zones_attach_reuse: An uploaded file can be attached to one post only; editing replaces the attachment list wholesale and removed files are deleted right away.
docs_page.zones_attach_login: All zone media (covers, images, videos, files) require a sign-in and follow the zone’s visibility.
docs_page.zones_embed_p1: Post and wiki bodies can embed site content natively: click “Embed” in the editor toolbar, search and pick in the dialog, and a preview card is inserted; in Markdown it is an own-line `[embed:kind:ref]` token.
docs_page.zones_embed_table:
| Token | Ref | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[embed:library:'<slug>']` | library document slug | Library |
| `[embed:short:'<id>']` | short video id | Shorts |
| `[embed:video:'<slug>']` | video slug | Videos |
| `[embed:skill:'<slug>']` | skill slug | Skills |
| `[embed:pack:'<slug>']` | pack slug | Skill packs |
| `[embed:event:'<id>']` | event id | Events |
| `[embed:post:'<id>']` | zone post id | Tech Zones |
| `[embed:file:'<id>']` | attachment id of this post | the current post’s attachments |
| `[embed:link:'<url>']` | full http / https URL | external link (title, description and image are fetched) |
docs_page.zones_embed_rule_line: A token must sit on its own line (at most 3 leading spaces); inside a paragraph it is not recognised.
docs_page.zones_embed_rule_fence: A token inside a code block (three backticks or three tildes) stays plain text; a 4-space indent counts as code too.
docs_page.zones_embed_rule_gate: Embeds obey the source’s own visibility: a library document, restricted skill or members-only zone post the reader may not see shows a “Content unavailable” card instead of its content.
docs_page.zones_embed_preview: Clicking a card opens the right-hand preview drawer — library documents read chapter by chapter, shorts and videos play inline, skills show the install command, events show time and venue, attachments show the PDF / image / slides; external links only show a link card and open in a new tab (the intranet blocks embedded pages).
docs_page.zones_embed_editor: In the editor an embed card shows a preview and “Remove”; it is always inserted at the top level after the current block, never inside a quote or list.
docs_page.zones_wiki_tree: Each zone has one wiki whose pages form a tree (left rail); holders of “Edit wiki” can add child pages and reorder or re-nest them with the up / down / indent buttons.
docs_page.zones_wiki_slug: Page URLs are /zones/'<zone>'/wiki/'<page slug>'; the slug is derived from the title (a CJK title gets a random slug), can be edited, and a duplicate inside the zone gets a -2, -3 suffix. Title up to 80 characters, body up to 200,000.
docs_page.zones_wiki_revisions: Every save creates a revision (a snapshot of title and body, with an optional note up to 120 characters); the page header shows the last editor, time and “Revision N”.
docs_page.zones_wiki_history: The “History” page lists every revision; open one to read the body as it was.
docs_page.zones_wiki_restore: “Restore this revision” saves the snapshot as a new revision (note auto-filled as “Restored from '<date>'”); history is never erased.
docs_page.zones_wiki_delete: Deleting a page is a soft delete; its child pages move up to the deleted page’s parent and are never lost.
docs_page.zones_wiki_perm: Reading the wiki follows the zone’s visibility; every write (create, edit, move, delete, restore) requires “Edit wiki”.
docs_page.zones_comments_levels: Two levels only: replying to a reply still attaches to that thread root — there is no third level — and the person you answered is still notified.
docs_page.zones_comments_who: Who may comment depends on the zone: members need “Comment” (the Member role has it by default); in a public zone with “Allow non-member comments” on, any signed-in user may comment.
docs_page.zones_comments_edit: The author can edit a comment for 15 minutes after posting (it shows “edited”); holders of “Moderate” can edit at any time.
docs_page.zones_comments_delete: Deleting a comment that has replies turns it into a “This comment was deleted” placeholder and keeps the replies; one without replies is removed outright. The author and holders of “Moderate” can delete.
docs_page.zones_comments_like: Comments can be liked and un-liked; body up to 3,000 characters.
docs_page.zones_comments_locked: A locked post refuses new comments (except from holders of “Moderate”); unlocking reopens it.
docs_page.zones_comments_notify: You get an in-app notification when someone comments on your post or replies to your comment (clicking it jumps to and highlights the entry); email is enabled under “Settings → Notifications”.

docs_page.zones_mod_delete: Posts and zones are soft-deleted: a post disappears from lists and search and the counters roll back; a deleted zone vanishes from the site together with its posts and wiki, and a site admin can restore it from the admin panel.
docs_page.zones_mod_admin: Every site-admin action inside a zone (and the admin panel’s create, feature, transfer, delete and restore) is written to the admin log.

docs_page.acct_home_intro: “Profile” in the avatar menu opens `/users/'<your staff ID>'`, which anyone can open without signing in. At the top, your card sits on the left; your name, headline, bio, badges, interests, links and stats are on the right. The stats only count sections the visitor is allowed to see. When you open your own profile, the top also offers Edit profile, Customize card, Sections & privacy and Visitor view.
docs_page.acct_home_tabs: The tabs below start with Overview (featured items, recent activity, About me and a section summary), followed by your content sections in the order you chose — Skills, Documents, Posts, Topics, Videos, Zones, Events, Votes, Feedback, Comments, Shelf — each listing everything of that kind you have published. Visitors never see an empty section; you keep them, with a link to go create something. The last tab, Workspace, is visible only to you.
docs_page.acct_home_pins: “Featured” at the top of Overview holds up to 6 items. On your own profile, Skills, documents, posts, topics, videos, zone posts, events and votes in the section tabs each carry a pin button; once 6 are pinned, unpin one first. Each visitor only sees the featured items they are allowed to see; the rest are skipped.
docs_page.acct_home_visitor: Visitor view adds `?as=visitor` to the address and shows your profile as an ordinary signed-in member sees it: hidden sections and the Workspace disappear, and a bar at the top says you are previewing as a visitor, with a link to exit. Anonymous visitors additionally miss the Videos, Zones and Votes sections and comments on library documents.
docs_page.acct_ws_redirect: The old `/dashboard` address still works and takes you to your Workspace; the avatar menu no longer has a dashboard entry. The six figures at the top of the Workspace jump to their sections, and longer lists fold the rest behind “Show N more”.
docs_page.acct_card_intro: Settings → Card (`/settings/card`) has the options on the left and a live preview on the right (above the options on a phone) that switches between “Card” and “On hover”. Pick the theme colour from 12 swatches or set your own (“Reset” returns to the colour generated from your name); add a status line (32 characters max) and a corner label for the mirror card (24 characters max); the “What to show” switches decide whether the card shows your department, badges and stats. With tilt on, the card follows the pointer only on devices with a mouse — on touch screens and with reduced motion enabled it stays still. Style, colour and text changes need “Save”. The three styles:
docs_page.acct_card_styles:
| Style | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| Holographic | Tilts with the pointer while a holographic sheen follows it; the sheen texture can be grid, dots, waves or none |
| Mirror | Your photo or video fills the card under a frosted-metal finish, laid out like an ID card; blur and grayscale are adjustable |
| Minimal | A card that follows the site’s light / dark theme, with your photo or video as a band at the top |
docs_page.acct_card_media: Photos: JPG / PNG / WebP / GIF, 10MB max. Except for GIFs, a photo is re-encoded in your browser as WebP or JPEG (at most 2048 px on the long edge) before upload: location, device model and other embedded metadata never leave your device, and the photo’s orientation is applied to the image itself. A GIF keeps its original file so the animation still plays. The server then strips any metadata that is left once more, keeping only the orientation tag. Videos: MP4 / WebM / MOV, 200MB max. Picking a video opens the “Trim your card video” window straight away while the original uploads in the background (the window shows the progress; “Cancel” stops the upload and nothing reaches your card). Drag the handles at either end of the timeline to set the start and end, or drag the middle to move the selection — 30 seconds at most, 1 second at least; a video shorter than 30 seconds is selected whole. The preview loops the selection muted (you can turn the sound on), and “Use this frame as cover” picks the cover — by default the frame half a second into the clip. On a keyboard, the arrow keys nudge by 0.1 s, or 1 s with Shift. Once the upload finishes, “Apply to card” has the server cut that range into a silent clip (sound and recording metadata removed, at most 720 px on the long edge) plus a cover at the chosen frame; your card loops the clip, so anything shorter than 30 seconds simply loops whole. The original video itself is never published — only you can reopen it, with “Trim clip”, to pick a different segment or cover without uploading again. If the server cannot cut clips at the moment, the card shows only the cover you chose. A video your browser cannot preview (some HEVC videos, for instance) uses its first 30 seconds when you confirm. With reduced motion enabled the card shows only the cover, and the trimmer preview does not autoplay. With a mouse, drag the picture on the preview card to reframe it; on a touch screen, tap “Reframe” under the preview first, then drag. A photo takes effect as soon as it uploads and a clip as soon as you apply it — no Save needed; “Remove” takes the media off the card.
docs_page.acct_card_hover: Your card appears in two places: at the top of your profile, and as the hover card other signed-in members see when they rest the pointer on your avatar. Anonymous visitors get no hover card. On a private account the card hides your @handle and department, except from administrators holding the identity permission. The “On hover” preview under Settings → Card shows the card exactly as an ordinary member sees it.
docs_page.acct_badges_intro: Badges on your card and profile come from three places: titles an administrator grants under 「用户标签」 in the admin console, titles the system grants automatically (such as 「版主」 for zone moderators), and honorary roles an administrator assigns you (such as 「专家」). Staff roles such as administrator never show as badges. Rest the pointer on a badge (or tap it on a touch screen) to see what the title means, where it came from and when you received it.
docs_page.acct_badges_hide: To stop showing a badge, hide it under Settings → My tags. You keep the badge and can show it again at any time.
